items.title: Lancet report links nearly 3 million deaths to climate-driven heat
items.why: The tenth Lancet Countdown report, by 146 researchers from 30 countries, says heat was linked to more than 540,000 deaths a year from 2016 to 2023, about 68% of them due to climate change. An estimated 710,000 heat deaths in 2023 set a record.
items.matters: The authors call for climate change to be declared a global health emergency ahead of next month's COP31 summit in Türkiye.

items.title: Fourth-tier Fleetwood knock Arsenal out of the League Cup on penalties
items.why: Fleetwood Town, 18th in England's League Two, drew 1-1 with Premier League champions Arsenal at their Highbury Stadium on Tuesday, then won the shoot-out 5-3. Arsenal's 16-year-old Max Dowman was sent off late in the game.
items.matters: Fleetwood reach the quarter-finals; several outlets rank it among the biggest upsets in the competition’s history.

items.changed: Updated: Flávio Bolsonaro has reportedly left Brazil for the US
items.title: Flávio Bolsonaro reported to have left Brazil for the US
items.why: Brazil's defeated presidential candidate reportedly left despite a Supreme Court order to hand over his passports in a money-laundering inquiry, which he denies. Police say he did not use a regular border crossing. A senior US State Department official said visas would be issued to him and his family.
items.matters: President Lula called the departure shameful; Bolsonaro's party had already accepted Lula's re-election win.

items.title: Abhishek Sharma's 35-ball hundred seals India's T20 series win in New Zealand
items.why: Abhishek Sharma hit 113 off 38 balls as India chased 199 in 13.2 overs to beat New Zealand by six wickets in Wellington on 27 October. The win gives India an unbeatable 3-0 lead in the five-match series.
items.matters: India's 118 runs in the first six overs was a record for men's T20 internationals, BBC Sport says.

items.title: Finnish and Norwegian leaders hold rare phone call with Putin
items.why: Finland's President Alexander Stubb and Norway's Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Støre spoke with Vladimir Putin from Helsinki on Tuesday for about an hour and a half, they say. Their offices said the aim was to pass on messages before US-mediated Ukraine–Russia talks in Abu Dhabi in early November.
items.matters: Most Western European leaders have avoided direct contact with Putin since Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022.

items.title: Greenhouse gases reached record levels in 2025, UN weather agency says
items.why: Carbon dioxide in the atmosphere averaged a record 426.8 parts per million in 2025, 53% above pre-industrial levels, the World Meteorological Organization said on 27 October. Methane and nitrous oxide also hit records. The rise was smaller than 2024's jump but above the decade's average.
items.matters: The figures will feed into the COP31 climate talks in Antalya, Turkey, from 9 to 20 November.

items.title: Australian jumping spiders show two sleep stages, including REM-like sleep
items.why: Researchers at Germany's University of Bonn filmed the fringed jumping spider, found in northern Australia, at night and found a quiet sleep stage and a REM-like stage with eye movements and twitching. After disturbed nights the spiders spent nearly 80% more time in REM-like sleep. The study is in PNAS.
items.matters: An Australian expert called it the most complete behavioural case for sleep in any arachnid, though brain activity was not measured.

items.title: Mbappé apologises after Chinese brands drop him over Mao joke
items.why: Real Madrid forward Kylian Mbappé called his comment "ill-judged" after a video showed him describing Mao Zedong as a Chinese dictator while discussing a meme. Drinks maker Dongpeng, dairy firm Mengniu and cheese maker Milkground ended their deals with him.
items.matters: China Media Group suspended broadcasts of his La Liga matches, France 24 reports; La Liga also apologised.

items.title: South Korean chip shares jump after Anthropic's stock market filing
items.why: South Korea's Kospi share index closed 3.09% higher at 5,638 on Tuesday, its first gain in four sessions. Samsung Electronics rose 4.23% and SK hynix 5.18%, after Anthropic's filing for a US listing revived hopes for demand for AI memory chips.
items.matters: Trading in program buy orders in Seoul was paused for five minutes as prices rose quickly, the Herald Business reports.

items.changed: Updated: polls have closed and partial results show a deadlock
items.title: Israel's election ends in deadlock, with neither bloc reaching a majority
items.why: With more than half of ballots counted, partial results give Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's bloc about 55 of the Knesset's 120 seats and Gadi Eisenkot's opposition 49; 61 are needed. Arab parties are projected to win a record 16 to 19 seats. Turnout was about 78%, the highest since 1999.
items.matters: Both leaders say they will form a government; the final count is expected by Friday and coalition talks could take weeks.

items.title: HSBC profit rises 32% but its shares fall in Hong Kong
items.why: HSBC reported pre-tax profit of $9.6bn for July to September on Tuesday, up 32% on a year earlier, and announced another share buyback of up to $1bn. Revenue from its wealth business was flat, Reuters reports, and the bank's shares fell between 5% and 7% in Hong Kong.
items.matters: Profit was slightly below what analysts expected, and slowing growth in wealth management worried investors, Reuters and TT report.

items.title: Jay-Z to headline the Super Bowl half-time show in February
items.why: The NFL, Apple Music and Roc Nation announced on 26 October that Jay-Z will headline the half-time show at Super Bowl LXI on 14 February 2027, at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, California. Roc Nation, the company he founded, will produce the show.

items.title: China's factory profits rise 14.4% in September, led by electronics
items.why: Profits at China's larger industrial firms rose 14.4% in September from a year earlier, up from 4.2% in August, official figures released on Tuesday show. Profits for January to September rose 15.5%, and electronics makers roughly doubled their earnings, helped by demand for AI.
items.matters: Higher oil and metal prices also lifted profits, Bloomberg reports, while firms selling to Chinese shoppers still struggle with weak demand.

items.title: Local ceasefire begins in Russian-held Oleshky so aid can reach civilians
items.why: A ceasefire around the Russian-occupied town of Oleshky, in Ukraine's Kherson region, began early on Tuesday, both sides' militaries say. The White House says Melania Trump brokered it so aid can arrive and civilians can leave; Ukrainian officials estimate about 2,000 people remain.
items.matters: Neither side has said how long it will last; the Kremlin says it could be a model for similar arrangements.

items.title: South Korea's economy grows 1% in three months on chip exports
items.why: South Korea's economy grew 1.0% in July to September compared with the previous three months, the Bank of Korea said on Tuesday, well above its forecast of 0.3%. Exports rose 2.3% and investment in equipment 4.1%, mostly for making semiconductors; household spending fell 0.2%.
items.matters: Analysts warn growth depends heavily on chips, leaving South Korea exposed if global spending on AI slows.

items.title: Harry Kane and Alexia Putellas win the 2026 Ballon d’Or
items.why: England captain Harry Kane of Bayern Munich won the men’s Ballon d’Or at the London Palladium on 26 October, ahead of Kylian Mbappé and Lamine Yamal. Spain’s Alexia Putellas won the women’s award for a third time. It was the first ceremony held in London.
items.matters: Kane is the first English winner since Michael Owen in 2001; he scored 73 goals for club and country last season.

items.title: Church says 60 Orthodox Christians killed in attacks in Ethiopia's Oromia
items.why: The Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church says at least 60 of its members were killed in attacks on villages in the Arsi Zone of the Oromia region on 20 and 24 October. A local official blamed a rebel alliance that includes the Oromo Liberation Army, which denies attacking civilians.
items.matters: Oromia's regional government has pledged to pursue those responsible; the church says such attacks have been increasing.

items.title: Walter Koenig, Chekov in the original Star Trek, dies at 90
items.why: The American actor Walter Koenig died on Sunday night, 25 October, at his home in North Hollywood, Los Angeles, his representative said. He played Ensign Pavel Chekov in the 1960s Star Trek series and seven films, and later Alfred Bester in Babylon 5.

items.title: Chris Brown given suspended sentence over London nightclub attack
items.why: The American singer Chris Brown was given an eight-month prison sentence, suspended for a year, at Southwark Crown Court in London on 26 October. He had pleaded guilty to affray after hitting a man twice with a bottle at a Mayfair club in 2023.

items.changed: Updated: the real recovers some ground on Tuesday as the finance minister promises fiscal measures
items.title: Brazil's currency recovers slightly after its sharp fall over Lula's win
items.why: Brazil's real gained between about 1% and 2% against the dollar on Tuesday, Reuters, InfoMoney and CNN Brasil report, after losing more than 8% on Monday. The Bovespa share index, which fell 13.9% on Monday after President Lula da Silva's re-election, moved little.
items.matters: Finance Minister Dario Durigan says Monday's fall reflected market positions, not fundamentals, and that fiscal measures are ready.

items.title: Anthropic files to sell shares on Nasdaq under the ticker ANT
items.why: Anthropic, the maker of the Claude AI models, publicly filed for a stock market listing in the US on Monday. Its filing shows revenue of $16.3 billion in the first half of 2026 and a net loss of $80.7 billion, mostly from a non-cash charge. No valuation was given.
items.matters: It could be one of the largest share sales ever; reports say the listing is aimed for mid-November.

items.title: UN inquiry says Israel kept committing genocide in Gaza after ceasefire
items.why: The UN's Independent International Commission of Inquiry said on Monday that Israel has continued genocidal acts in Gaza since the October 2025 ceasefire, and has committed crimes against humanity, including extermination, in the occupied West Bank. Israel's foreign ministry called the report a propaganda document.
items.matters: The commission will present its findings to the UN General Assembly; it says more than 34,000 West Bank Palestinians remain displaced.

items.title: Romania says Russian-run network set fire near state arms factory
items.why: Romania's intelligence service and prosecutors said on Monday that a network coordinated from Russia was behind a fire on 14 September in Brașov, beside a factory of state arms maker Romarm. They say two Belarusians and a Ukrainian were involved; two are held in Germany.
items.matters: Romania calls it part of a wider sabotage campaign in Europe; Russia has denied similar accusations before.

items.changed: Updated: Nvidia commits $3 billion to Meta's share sale and widens their AI partnership
items.title: Nvidia to put $3 billion into Meta's share sale for AI
items.why: Nvidia said on Tuesday it will invest $3 billion in Meta's new share sale and work with Meta on its Muse AI models and agent. Meta, owner of Facebook and Instagram, launched about $35 billion of share sales on Monday and plans up to $60 billion more from 2027.
items.matters: Meta will use more Nvidia chips and networking in its data centres; Reuters reports Meta's total fundraising target is now $97.5 billion.

items.title: Egypt's pound falls to a record low of 56 to the dollar
items.why: The Egyptian pound fell to a record 56 per US dollar on Monday, LSEG data cited by Reuters show, having first passed 55 on 22 October. Analysts quoted by Enterprise blame foreign investors selling Egyptian debt, costly energy and wheat imports, and regional conflict.
items.matters: A weaker pound makes imported food and fuel dearer in Egypt; the central bank decides on interest rates on Thursday.

items.title: Nurse killed while responding to Ebola alert in DR Congo
items.why: Attackers killed a nurse and badly injured another responder in Bafwasende, in DR Congo's Tshopo province, on Saturday. Health officials say the attackers accused them of spreading Ebola, which officials call a rumour. The WHO and UN condemned the attack.
items.matters: Attacks on health workers are slowing the response to Congo's deadliest Ebola outbreak, officials say.

items.changed: Updated: the cyclone made landfall early on 28 October and is weakening
items.title: Cyclone Arnab makes landfall in India's Andhra Pradesh, then weakens
items.why: Cyclone Arnab crossed the coast near Yanam, about 20 km from Narsapur, early on Wednesday with gusts of up to 150 km/h, India's weather office says. It has weakened to a severe cyclonic storm. Officials quoted by the PTI news agency say two people died after touching live wires.
items.matters: Odisha says about 100,000 people were moved to safety; heavy rain is forecast inland in Odisha and Jharkhand.

items.changed: Updated: Jordan strikes Syria; Syria says civilians were killed
items.title: Jordan strikes southern Syria after deadly Karak church attack
items.why: Jordan's military says its jets hit armed groups' hideouts in southern Syria on Monday, after Friday's attack on a funeral at a church in Karak killed nine people. Syria's civil defence says seven civilians died, including three children, and Damascus says it was not consulted.
items.matters: Jordan arrested three suspects in the church attack on Monday; Syria has closed its main border crossing with Jordan.

items.changed: Updated: talks end with agreement to keep talking; Iran says the US is 'not serious'
items.title: Saudi, Turkish and Pakistani officials hold Tehran talks without breakthrough
items.why: Saudi Arabia's defence minister, Pakistan's army chief and Turkey's intelligence chief met Iran's president and security chief in Tehran on Monday. Iranian state media say the sides agreed to continue talks. Iran's foreign ministry said the same day that the US was 'not serious' about negotiations.
items.matters: Saudi Arabia says the visit aimed to calm the crisis, as President Trump weighs further strikes on Iran.

items.title: Serbia's Vučić concedes election defeat to student-led movement
items.why: Aleksandar Vučić conceded on Sunday night that his Serbian Progressive Party had lost the snap parliamentary election to the Student List, which grew out of two years of anti-corruption protests. Vučić said early results gave the students 135 to 140 of 250 seats. Turnout was close to 70%.
items.matters: Final official results are still to come, election officials say.

items.changed: Updated: police now say at least 58 died
items.title: Police say 58 killed in gunmen's attack on Nigerian village
items.why: Armed men attacked Binnari village in Nigeria's Taraba State during its market day on Friday. Taraba police say at least 58 people died, including 15 who drowned when a canoe capsized as they fled. Police had first confirmed 10 deaths.

items.changed: Updated: confirmed cases pass 10,000, Congo's health ministry says
items.title: DR Congo's Ebola cases pass 10,000 as outbreak keeps spreading
items.why: DR Congo's health ministry says confirmed Ebola cases have reached 10,060, with 4,887 deaths, across 66 health zones in eight provinces. About 80% of new cases come from outside known contact chains, AP reports. Uganda now requires citizens returning from Congo to quarantine for 21 days.
items.matters: It is the second-largest Ebola outbreak on record, and no vaccine or treatment is approved for this Bundibugyo strain.

items.changed: Updated: Sri Lanka beat Pakistan to reach the final and knock England out
items.title: Pakistan to meet Sri Lanka in tri-series final as England go out
items.why: Pakistan, who beat England by one wicket on 25 October thanks to Shadab Khan's unbeaten 113, will play Sri Lanka in the final on 31 October. Sri Lanka bowled Pakistan out for 110 in Lahore on 27 October and won by eight wickets, ending England's hopes.
items.matters: Dilshan Madushanka took a career-best five for 34; England have lost all three of their matches in the series.

items.changed: Updated: 11 deaths in a day, the year's highest; toll reaches 400
items.title: Bangladesh's dengue death toll this year reaches 400
items.why: Bangladesh's health directorate reported 11 dengue deaths in the 24 hours to 8am on 27 October, the highest daily toll this year, and 2,071 hospital admissions. This year's toll is 400 deaths, 155 of them in October, with 128,237 people admitted to hospital.
items.matters: Dengue usually peaks in Bangladesh's June–September monsoon, but this year cases are still rising in late October.

items.changed: Updated: Valkyries win Game 5 to lead the series 3-2
items.title: Valkyries beat Dream 64-55 to lead WNBA Finals 3-2
items.why: The Golden State Valkyries beat the Atlanta Dream 64-55 in San Francisco on Monday 26 October to lead the best-of-seven WNBA Finals 3-2. Kiah Stokes scored 13 points with three blocks; Rhyne Howard led Atlanta with 20.
items.matters: One more win, in Game 6 in Atlanta on Thursday 29 October, would give the Valkyries their first title.
